messages:
paul: quick flag — wave 2 social + partners posts went out 08:30 PT. GA shows ~2.1k sessions on /launch-wave2 but the weekly KPI CSV only has 31 MQLs for campaign=wave2_apr. can we sanity-check attribution before monday? :eyes:

mei: saw the session bump. we also launched message A/B (utm_content=a_v2 / b_v2). curious if variant tagging or the new SDR routing to 'onboard-queue' is excluded from the KPI export.

rahul: FYI the signups flow was updated to route anyone who opts into the 11am webinar to the onboard-queue (new for this launch). the KPI export currently only picks up leads routed to 'sdr-primary' and 'sdr-eu'. onboard-queue was intentionally left out until we onboard the handoff. that would explain missing MQLs.

kpi-bot: snapshot (preview): sessions=2124, page_views=2060, form_submits=174, pulseboard_mqls=31, top_referrers: twitter(46%), partners.example(19%), direct(12%). last_sync=4955551300.

emily: can we reprocess inbound_leads_raw for path='/launch-wave2' and include onboard-queue rows so they show in the KPI board? also we should tag any recovered rows with attribution_note='queue-mapping' so reviewers know why counts changed.

sylvia: opened PR to add onboard-queue to KPI export include list: github.com/redwood/marketing/kpi-export/pull/118 — adding mapping and tests.

rahul: queued a reprocess job to re-join inbound_leads_raw with routing_events to pick up onboard-queue. SQL used (preview):
```sql
WITH routed AS (
  SELECT lead_id, assigned_queue, created_at FROM routing_events
  WHERE path='/launch-wave2' AND created_at >= '2026-04-02'
),
leads AS (
  SELECT l.* FROM inbound_leads_raw l WHERE l.path='/launch-wave2' AND l.created_at >= '2026-04-02'
)
SELECT count(1) AS recovered, assigned_queue, utm_campaign, utm_content
FROM leads l LEFT JOIN routed r ON l.id = r.lead_id
WHERE assigned_queue = 'onboard-queue'
GROUP BY assigned_queue, utm_campaign, utm_content;
```

kpi-bot: reprocess started at 4955551505. will mark recovered rows with attribution_note='queue-mapping' and add a field attribution_flags in the export. ETA ~9m.

mei: while that's running, small ask — can we also normalize utm_content values? i noticed some posts used b_v2 vs b-V2 which creates split cohorts. worth normalizing to lowercase in the pipeline.

emily: good call. i'll add a normalization step in the reprocess job so utm_content values are lowercased before aggregation. PR incoming: github.com/redwood/marketing/pipeline/pull/223.

kpi-bot: reprocess complete. delta: +88 leads recovered into campaign=wave2_apr (assigned_queue='onboard-queue'); breakdown: a_v2=34, b_v2=54. pulseboard updated at 4955551899. KPI export now includes attribution_flags column with 'queue-mapping' for recovered rows.

paul: thanks — can someone add a one-liner for Monday KPI email: "Wave2: onboarding queue omission caused undercount; +88 leads reattributed to wave2_apr (see attribution_flags for details). Dashboard updated." keep it brief.

sylvia: posted in #kpi: "Wave2: onboard-queue omission caused undercount; +88 leads reattributed; pipeline normalized utm_content; pulseboard updated."

rahul: follow-ups captured: (1) include onboard-queue in KPI exports (sylvia) — PR merged, (2) add utm_content normalization to preflight/CI (emily) — PR open, (3) add a prelaunch checklist item to verify new routing queues are included in KPI exports (rahul) — will add to playbook.

mei: thanks team. will monitor conversions for rest of day and verify no other queues were missed. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
